proposals.before: Yanzhang rushed to attack, as Chongtao had foreseen. In the midsummer heat his men dropped dead; they failed to take the fort and lost more than half their strength. As they hurried back toward Yangliu, Zhuangzong met them and broke them.
proposals.after: Yanzhang rushed to attack. In the midsummer heat his men dropped dead; they failed to take the fort and lost more than half their strength. As they hurried back toward Yangliu, Zhuangzong met them and broke them.
proposals.reason: The Chinese does not mention Chongtao or foresight in this sentence; the idiomatic line invents that clause.

proposals.before: Chongtao grew afraid and confided in the sons of old friends: “I helped the emperor win the realm. The great work is done, and petty men are closing in. I want to withdraw to Zhenyuan and try to dodge ruin—is that wise?”
proposals.after: Chongtao grew afraid and confided in the sons of old friends: “I helped the emperor win the realm. The great work is done, and petty men are closing in. I want to withdraw to Zhenyang and try to dodge ruin—is that wise?”
proposals.reason: Chinese 鎮陽 is Zhenyang (the Chengde seat), not Zhenyuan.

proposals.before: Chongtao grew quite afraid and told the sons of old friends: “I aided the Son of Heaven in taking the realm. Now the great work is done and petty men rise together. I wish to withdraw, return to guard Zhenyuan, and perhaps escape disaster—is that possible?”
proposals.after: Chongtao grew quite afraid and told the sons of old friends: “I aided the Son of Heaven in taking the realm. Now the great work is done and petty men rise together. I wish to withdraw, return to guard Zhenyang, and perhaps escape disaster—is that possible?”
proposals.reason: Chinese 鎮陽 is Zhenyang, not Zhenyuan.

proposals.before: Chongtao memorialized again and again, asking to restore the old Tang practice of putting eunuchs back in the Privy Commission and to be released from Zhenyuan. The court answered with a gracious refusal.
proposals.after: Chongtao memorialized again and again, asking to restore the old Tang practice of putting eunuchs back in the Privy Commission and to be released from Zhenyang. The court answered with a gracious refusal.
proposals.reason: Chinese 鎮陽 is Zhenyang, not Zhenyuan.

proposals.before: Chongtao repeatedly memorialized on his own behalf, asking to restore the Tang custom of returning the Privy Commission to inner courtiers, and at the same time declined Zhenyuan—a gracious edict would not allow it.
proposals.after: Chongtao repeatedly memorialized on his own behalf, asking to restore the Tang custom of returning the Privy Commission to inner courtiers, and at the same time declined Zhenyang—a gracious edict would not allow it.
proposals.reason: Chinese 鎮陽 is Zhenyang, not Zhenyuan.

proposals.before: Quanyi was furious and sent men to Empress Liu to plead Guan’s case in soft words. Meanwhile the emperor’s attendants spent day and night picking at Guan’s every flaw.
proposals.after: Quanyi was furious and sent men to Empress Liu to lay out Guan’s offenses in mild words. Meanwhile the emperor’s attendants spent day and night picking at Guan’s every flaw.
proposals.reason: Angry 白貫事 is a complaint against Guan, not a plea on his behalf.

proposals.before: Quanyi was greatly angered and once sent men to tell Empress Liu, gently pleading Guan’s case—but the emperor’s attendants day and night jointly attacked Guan’s faults.
proposals.after: Quanyi was greatly angered and once sent men to tell Empress Liu, calmly stating Guan’s offenses—but the emperor’s attendants day and night jointly attacked Guan’s faults.
proposals.reason: 白貫事 reports Guan’s conduct to the empress after Quanyi’s anger; it is not a plea for Guan.

proposals.before: When the army reached Chengdu, Zongbi moved Yan to the western palace and sent Yan’s concubines, entertainers, and treasures to Chongtao and his son Yanhui.
proposals.after: When the army reached Chengdu, Zongbi moved Yan to the western palace and sent Yan’s concubines, entertainers, and treasures to Chongtao and his son Tinghui.
proposals.reason: 廷誨 is Tinghui, not Yanhui.

proposals.before: When the army reached Chengdu, Zongbi moved Yan to the western palace and gathered Yan’s concubines, entertainers, and treasures to present to Chongtao and his son Yanhui.
proposals.after: When the army reached Chengdu, Zongbi moved Yan to the western palace and gathered Yan’s concubines, entertainers, and treasures to present to Chongtao and his son Tinghui.
proposals.reason: 廷誨 is Tinghui, not Yanhui.

proposals.before: When Liang attacked Zhu Xuan at Yanzhou, Jin troops went to rescue him; Xuan was defeated and Fu Qian died in battle.
proposals.after: When Liang attacked Zhu Xuan at Yunzhou, Jin troops went to rescue him; Xuan was defeated and Fu Qian died in battle.
proposals.reason: 鄆州 is Yunzhou, not Yanzhou (兗州).

proposals.before: When Liang attacked Zhu Xuan at Yan prefecture, Jin troops went to rescue Xuan; Xuan was defeated and Fu Qian died in battle.
proposals.after: When Liang attacked Zhu Xuan at Yun prefecture, Jin troops went to rescue Xuan; Xuan was defeated and Fu Qian died in battle.
proposals.reason: 鄆州 should be rendered Yun prefecture, not Yan prefecture.

proposals.before: Li Renfu of Xias prefecture presented a white hawk; Chonghui refused it. The next day he reported: “Your Majesty has decreed that none under heaven may present hawks and falcons, yet Renfu defied the decree and presented a hawk; your servant has already refused it.”
proposals.after: Li Renfu of Xia prefecture presented a white hawk; Chonghui refused it. The next day he reported: “Your Majesty has decreed that none under heaven may present hawks and falcons, yet Renfu defied the decree and presented a hawk; your servant has already refused it.”
proposals.reason: 夏州 is Xia prefecture; “Xias” is a corrupted spelling.

proposals.before: Li Renfu of Xias prefecture presented a white hawk; Chonghui refused it; the next day he reported to the throne: “Your Majesty has decreed that none under heaven may present hawks and falcons, yet Renfu defied the decree and presented a hawk; your servant has already refused it.”
proposals.after: Li Renfu of Xia prefecture presented a white hawk; Chonghui refused it; the next day he reported to the throne: “Your Majesty has decreed that none under heaven may present hawks and falcons, yet Renfu defied the decree and presented a hawk; your servant has already refused it.”
proposals.reason: 夏州 is Xia prefecture; “Xias” is a corrupted spelling.

proposals.before: Tian Lingfang, horse-pasture commissioner, tended horses that were gaunt and many died; impeached, he merited death; Chonghui remonstrated: “If all under heaven hear that for a horse’s sake a commissioner was killed, they will say we value beasts and cheapen men.
proposals.after: Tian Lingfang, horse-pasture commissioner, tended horses that were gaunt and many died; impeached, he merited death; Chonghui remonstrated: “If all under heaven hear that for a horse’s sake a commissioner was killed, they will say we value beasts and cheapen men.”
proposals.reason: The quoted remonstrance is left unclosed in the literal English.

proposals.before: When Mei returned he slandered Zhaoyu to Chonghui: “Zhaoyu saw Liu, bowed in dance and called himself subject, and privately told Liu court affairs.
proposals.after: When Mei returned he slandered Zhaoyu to Chonghui: “Zhaoyu saw Liu, bowed in dance and called himself subject, and privately told Liu court affairs.”
proposals.reason: The quoted slander is left unclosed in the literal English.

proposals.before: Congke fled to Yu village and sent riders to report the crisis.
proposals.after: Congke fled to Yuxiang and sent riders to report the crisis.
proposals.reason: 虞鄉 is the county name Yuxiang, not a village called Yu.

proposals.before: Mingzong doubted the affair was unclear and wished to get to the bottom of it. He sent the palace attendant Fan Hun with a gold belt, surcoat, gold saddle, and bridle as gifts to Yanwen and made Yanwen prefect of Jiangzhou to lure him in.
proposals.after: Mingzong suspected the affair was unclear and wished to get to the bottom of it. He sent the palace attendant Fan Hun with a gold belt, surcoat, gold saddle, and bridle as gifts to Yanwen and made Yanwen prefect of Jiangzhou to lure him in.
proposals.reason: 疑其事不明 means he thought the matter was not clear; “doubted the affair was unclear” reverses the sense with a double negative.

proposals.before: Mingzong said: “When I was a petty officer I could not feed myself. This boy carried lime and gathered horse dung to keep me alive—now he is exalted as Son of Heaven, and I cannot shelter him?
proposals.after: Mingzong said: “When I was a petty officer I could not feed myself. This boy carried lime and gathered horse dung to keep me alive—now that I am exalted as Son of Heaven, can I not shelter him?
proposals.reason: 今貴為天子 is Mingzong speaking of himself as emperor, not Congke; the English makes Congke the Son of Heaven.

proposals.before: Congke’s generation kept the practice; affairs split in two—civil work to the chancellors, military work to the Privy Council.
proposals.after: Succeeding generations kept the practice; affairs split in two—civil work to the chancellors, military work to the Privy Council.
proposals.reason: Chinese 從世 means succeeding ages/generations; the current English treats it as the personal name Congke, which is captured as p013’s English alias pending this repair.

proposals.before: Congke’s generation continued it; affairs were then split in two—civil matters to the chancellors, military matters to the Privy Council.
proposals.after: Succeeding generations continued it; affairs were then split in two—civil matters to the chancellors, military matters to the Privy Council.
proposals.reason: Chinese 從世 means succeeding ages/generations; the current English treats it as the personal name Congke, which is captured as p013’s English alias pending this repair.

decisions.after: Yanzhang indeed rushed to attack. In the midsummer heat his men dropped dead; they failed to take the fort and lost more than half their strength. As they hurried back toward Yangliu, Zhuangzong met them and broke them.
decisions.reason: The sentence does not name Chongtao or ascribe foresight to him, so that clause must go; 果 still marks the attack as happening as expected and should be kept.
